findings.counterexample: run_presubmit compiles only mission.valid.json, invokes the V16 checker directly, and compiles a fresh archive; it never drives GateRunner, readiness transitions, evidence-envelope validation, Spark-result validation, or collect_metrics. A malformed gate/state/evidence/Spark/metric boundary can therefore leave the advertised one-command presubmit GREEN.
findings.label: BLOCKING

findings.counterexample: Add a blocking invariant that references an existing counterexample but has no acceptance row, or make G-FRESH depend directly on G-TARGETED while retaining an unrelated G-FULL. The linkage/compiler checks accept both mutations, so an invariant can be non-executable and fresh readiness can bypass the full stage.
findings.label: BLOCKING

findings.counterexample: An entrypoint argv of ["/bin/sh","-c","echo unsafe"] compiles because the deny-list compares only the exact first token "sh"/"bash"/... and does not normalize executable basenames. The resulting shell invocation can enter a plan advertised as direct argv with shell=false.
findings.label: BLOCKING

findings.counterexample: A legal transition sequence can keep green_counterexamples empty, disposition a Spark P1 as FOLLOW_UP, and then supply arbitrary evidence_ids=["FAKE"], gate_ids=["FAKE"], and review_ready=True. The state machine reaches REVIEW_READY without same-ID candidate GREEN results, closed blockers, validated receipts, or an independent review artifact.
findings.label: BLOCKING

findings.counterexample: The runner checks HEAD/tree/dirty only before entrypoint execution and never rechecks after execution. A checker can mutate a tracked file or HEAD and emit valid GREEN counts, yet the gate returns allow with stale pre-run identity. Separately, validate_gate_result accepts an empty actual_head and any non-empty 40-hex tree_sha without binding either to expected identity.
findings.label: BLOCKING

findings.counterexample: Each child receives os.environ.copy() with only proxy keys removed, logs are written without privacy scanning, and timeout handling does not create/own a process group or terminate descendants. A checker can exfiltrate an inherited secret to stderr, open a socket, or leave a background child alive after timeout while the gate still records an otherwise valid result.
findings.label: BLOCKING
